code: library(seqsalvage)  reads <- read_spf("project.SPF") reads[[1]]$name substr(reads[[1]]$bases, 1, 60) matplot(reads[[1]]$traces[1:600, ], type = "l", lty = 1, col = c("green3", "blue", "black", "red"))  # write every read in the project as an .ab1 file spf_to_abif("project.SPF", "recovered_traces")  # also fill the base-caller tags, so Biopython and sangerseqR can read the files spf_to_abif("project.SPF", "recovered_traces", basecaller = TRUE)  # include reads deleted from the project whose data is still in the file deleted <- Filter(function(r) r$deleted, read_spf("project.SPF", deleted = TRUE))  # contigs: name, saved consensus and member reads contigs <- read_spf_contigs("project.SPF") contigs[[1]]$name contigs[[1]]$reads  # write each contig's saved consensus to a FASTA file spf_contigs_to_fasta("project.SPF", "contigs.fasta")

text: ABIF keeps two sets base calls: PBAS1, PCON1 PLOC1 hold calls, quality scores peak positions edited user, PBAS2, PCON2 PLOC2 hold called base caller. Sequencher project keeps edited set, record reads edited, default write_abif() fills edited tags. readers need base-caller tags.
